exports.text: Header supplies addressing plus decoding interface for covered hub registers: per-register offset selectors, per-field shift and mask values, and whole-word versus bitfield overlay types for driver use.

hazards.text: Identical offsets mean different blocks or events on different generations and families, so decoding with the wrong generation view misattributes errors and interrupts. Callers must select the overlay matching probed hardware before interpreting any word.

Some logical indicators move across generations; one clock indicator lives at different positions on newer versus older hardware. A negative shift signals absence rather than a usable position and reserved upper bits carry no meaning, so callers must treat the unknown-generation sentinel as invalid and mask or preserve reserved bits on update.

Address selection differs on unknown hardware: the GAM configuration selector can silently yield zero and risk access to the wrong register, whereas TLB interrupt selectors route through an explicit undefined marker. Callers must validate generation and must not assume a valid address without it.

invariants.text: Every event indicator is a one-bit readable writable field packed in increasing order from the least significant end; each mask isolates exactly the bit named by its companion shift and reserved fields only pad the view to the full 64-bit width.
Shifts within each interrupt family increase by one with no gaps or overlaps and all observed word-one positions fall within the low fifty-two bits of the word.

Generic position and mask selectors are generation sensitive. External line zero is bit one on generation five and absent otherwise; one clock indicator uses mask eight and position three on five, single bit nineteen on four, single bit one on three and two, and zero mask with negative-one shift when unknown. Consumers must branch on probed generation before shifting.

In TLB interrupt configuration words vector, delivery and destination mode, mask and APIC identifier are writable while status and delivery-state indicators are read-only; positions and widths are identical across groups, indices and revisions. Small controls live at fixed positions such as broadcast enable at bit zero and subspace control at bit ten.

structs.text: Event status word zero is one 64-bit container with distinct per-generation overlays. The routed window shows the tail of a newer view plus complete older views for successive hardware levels. Each complete view packs single-bit flags for per-block hard and always-on errors, shutdown, sixteen local interrupts, nonmaskable, clock stop, bidirectional bridge signals, trigger, interprocessor and external inputs plus reserved padding. Newer and older views differ in which block each early offset tracks and in trailing profiling and reserved treatment.

Event word one is a 64-bit word readable as a plain scalar or through alternative single-bit overlays for a common view and generations five through two. Common and generation-five overlays share thirty-eight low signals in order: interprocessor, four external lines, profiler, broadcast data, general processor, six crossbar lines and twenty-four remote-directory lines with twenty-six reserved high bits. Generation four starts with profiler, broadcast and general flags then twenty-four group-zero plus twenty-four group-one lines with thirteen reserved bits. Generations three and two share broadcast data, power request, sixteen accelerator, sixteen group-zero, sixteen group-one, interval and dashboard flags with twelve reserved bits.

In the common family layout of word one the lowest eight positions each carry one system event in ascending order: interprocessor, four external inputs, profiling, broadcast data and general processor. The next six consecutive positions carry coherence events for one translation block, followed by twenty-four consecutive events for a second larger translation block, each with its own shift and one-bit mask pair.

For generations three and two the low allocation is dense: broadcast data at zero, power request at one, accelerator interrupts zero through fifteen at two through seventeen, group-zero zero through fifteen at eighteen through thirty-three, group-one zero through fifteen at thirty-four through forty-nine, interval at fifty and dashboard at fifty-one. The generation-four tail holds group-one interrupts two through twenty-three at twenty-nine through fifty in steps of one.

Fixed hub offsets include event-zero alias at 0x70008, event-one at 0x70080, event-one alias at 0x70088, event-two at 0x70100, plus single constant offsets for event-two alias, external broadcast, compare B and IPI. GR0 GAM GR configuration selects one smaller offset on newer generations and a larger offset on older ones with zero fallback. GR0 and GR1 TLB interrupt configuration offsets are generation selected, with one pair shared across three older generations and the other split across generations.

Second event status is a 64-bit scalar with generation-specific overlays splitting the same bits into named one-bit indicators plus reserved high padding ordered from least significant upward. Common views place interval at zero, dashboard at one and thirty-two clocks at two through thirty-three with thirty reserved bits. Generation four places sixteen accelerator indicators at zero through fifteen, interval at sixteen, dashboard at seventeen and thirty-two clocks at eighteen through forty-nine with fourteen reserved bits. Generations three and two place thirty-two clocks at zero through thirty-one with the upper half reserved.

External broadcast is a 64-bit word with a single writable enable at bit zero and the remainder reserved across all revision views. GR0 GAM GR configuration is 64-bit with revision-specific views: common and newer expose only a writable subspace control in the low bits, one older view adds a writable socket field plus a hole, and the oldest exposes a small group-count field. Each TLB interrupt configuration word shares one layout across groups, indices and revisions: low vector selector, delivery and destination controls, status, mask, gaps and a wide APIC destination in the upper half. Compare B holds a wide writable real-time compare value in the lower majority with a small reserved top.
